evidence_basis_note: DFAPTA (Deep Forensic All Paths Taken Analysis) is an iterative, multi-pass process, not a single-shot synthesis - see DEC-0007. This is Pass 1: every distinct claim, account, comparator and mechanism in the frozen evidence register (EV-0001 through EV-0023, DEC-0006) is given its own dedicated path rather than compressed into a smaller number of thematic summaries. A prior nine-path pass was removed for being generic and incomplete. Further passes continue until the operator states DFAPTA itself is frozen - that freeze is a separate, later event from DEC-0006, and no downstream stage (SHM Gate, Lattice Atlas, Temporal Projection Integrity Engine, Enforcement Notice, Advocacy Package) is built until it happens. Both CTR-0001 and CTR-0002 were Open at freeze and are carried forward here as unresolved.

paths.title: Rudder Park — the In-Shire Precedent
analysis: Kempsey Shire Council completed a Flying-fox Camp Management Plan for Rudder Park, East Kempsey, in 2022 (EV-0002) - the shire's only completed plan for any site. Access to the NSW Government's roughly $1 million flying-fox camp management grants program requires a completed or draft plan for the specific site (EV-0011). No plan exists, or is in draft, for Bellbrook (EV-0017).

This is not a claim that the mechanism is unfamiliar to this council. Rudder Park demonstrates Kempsey Shire Council already knows how to produce this exact instrument, has produced it once, and therefore is not blocked by unfamiliarity with the process itself.
determinations: The absence of a Bellbrook plan cannot be explained by the council's lack of experience with the instrument - it has produced one, for a different site in the same shire, as recently as 2022.
paths.boundary: Does not establish why Rudder Park received a plan and Bellbrook has not - no comparative site-selection criteria appear anywhere in this case's register.

paths.title: The NSW Grant Program's Plan-Gating Rule — Claimed but Not Yet Sighted
analysis: The central structural claim in this case - that a completed or draft Camp Management Plan is a strict precondition for grant access - rests entirely on operator-supplied fact sheets (EV-0002, EV-0011), not on the program's own published guidelines. No primary DCCEEW document stating this rule has been retrieved by this case.
determinations: This case's single most load-bearing claim - that the plan is a strict funding gate, not merely a favourable factor - is currently a secondary-source claim, not a confirmed one.
paths.boundary: Q-0002 remains open. Every downstream path that treats the plan as "the" funding precondition (AR-001, AR-003, AR-004) inherits this same unconfirmed status and should not be read as more certain than this path establishes.

paths.title: Townsville — External Comparator, Active Revision
analysis: On 1 April 2026, Townsville City Council unanimously adopted a revised Flying-Fox Management Plan covering 16 recorded roosts, adding active dispersal as a feasibility option for the first time, following 2024 community consultation in which 60% of survey respondents agreed flying-foxes should be managed and 54% described living near them as a serious problem (EV-0020, CHR-0010). This is a different state-region council, in a different jurisdiction context, actively operating and revising the exact instrument absent for Bellbrook.
determinations: The management-plan mechanism is not a rare, one-off instrument confined to a single site - a comparable regional council actively revises one, in the same month this case was frozen.
paths.boundary: Townsville is a substantially larger council with a different resourcing base than Kempsey Shire - this path does not claim the two councils are directly comparable in capacity, only that the instrument itself is neither exotic nor abandoned as a governance tool.

paths.title: Mount Isa — External Comparator, Funded Specifically for Development
analysis: Mount Isa City Council published public consultation on 14 January 2026 for a new Flying-Fox Management Plan, developed with support from the Queensland Government's Flying-Fox Roost Management Local Government Grant Program - a four-year, $2 million initiative extended by a further $1.5 million, administered by DETSI (EV-0021, CHR-0011). This is the clearest available evidence that state/territory-level funding exists specifically to pay for plan development itself, not only for implementing an already-completed plan.
determinations: A 'no budget to even start a plan' justification is undercut by a real, funded state-level mechanism existing specifically to cover the development cost - in a different state (Queensland, not NSW), which limits how directly this precedent transfers, but which establishes the development-funding gap is not universal or unaddressable in principle.
paths.boundary: This is a Queensland DETSI program, not a NSW DCCEEW one - it demonstrates the concept of development-stage funding exists somewhere, not that an equivalent NSW mechanism is confirmed to exist (see AR-002, Q-0002).

paths.title: 20 May 2025 Meeting — Account One: Decline on Budget Grounds
analysis: Seven of the original eight operator-supplied documents, and the independently-fetched Macleay Argus article (EV-0001), describe Kempsey Shire Council stating at the 20 May 2025 meeting that it "simply does not have the budget to tackle the issue," with a separate, informal indication it hoped to revisit the matter at the October 2025 meeting. No resolution number or recorded vote is reported in this account (EV-0001, EV-0003 in part).
determinations: This is the account with the broadest independent sourcing in the case - it is the only one of the three competing accounts corroborated by a source this repository fetched and read directly, rather than one supplied or relayed by the operator.
paths.boundary: Does not itself establish this account is the accurate one - only that it is the most independently corroborated of the three (see AR-008).

paths.title: 20 May 2025 Meeting — Account Two: Numbered Resolution, 9/0 Vote
analysis: The Hardened Submission Package (EV-0010) describes a specific, numbered sequence: Resolution 2025.79 (extending meeting hours), a shire-wide-alignment amendment defeated 2/7, and Resolution 2025.80 passed 9/0, directing executive investigation of Level 1 management options and a report back by the October meeting. This is the case's most legally load-bearing account - it is what the Hardened Submission Package's SafeWork NSW and Office of Local Government submissions rest on, since it characterises the October failure as non-execution of an affirmative unanimous directive rather than a discretionary refusal.

No other document in this case - including EV-0001, the one independently-fetched source - mentions any resolution number or vote count. A targeted search for these specific resolution numbers found no corroboration; both Council's own site and web.archive.org blocked automated fetch of the primary minutes.
determinations: This account carries the most specific factual detail of the three - and the least independent corroboration. It should not be repeated as fact in any public-facing material until the signed minutes are obtained (see EV-0010's own recorded caution, and Enforcement Notice guidance if this case's remedy documents are rebuilt).
paths.boundary: Explicitly does not conclude this account is inaccurate - only that it is currently uncorroborated, which is a different and weaker claim than false.

paths.title: 20 May 2025 Meeting — Account Three: Operator-Relayed Bridging Account
analysis: Operator-relayed research supplied 2026-08-23 (EV-0014, citation not yet provided) states Council unanimously resolved in May 2025 to hold a Bellbrook community meeting, investigate management options, and report back - without stating a resolution number or vote count. This does not match Account One's flat-decline framing, and does not match Account Two's specific numbers, but agrees with Account Two that some affirmative resolution occurred, and is silent on the numbers Account Two supplies.
determinations: This account is consistent with, but does not independently confirm, either of the other two - it narrows the live dispute to a question of specific figures (Account Two's numbers) rather than resolving whether an affirmative resolution occurred at all.
paths.boundary: Supplied without a citation - this is operator-relayed, not independently located by this repository, and carries a correspondingly lower evidentiary weight than EV-0001.

paths.title: Triangulating the Three Meeting Accounts
analysis: What actually followed the 20 May 2025 meeting - a council-organised community meeting on 27 August 2025 and door-to-door resident visits on 16 September 2025 (EV-0004, CHR-0004, CHR-0005) - reads more naturally as fulfilling a resolution to investigate and report back than as unprompted goodwill following a flat decline. This lends some circumstantial weight to Accounts Two and Three over Account One's pure-decline framing, without confirming Account Two's specific resolution numbers.

The three accounts are not symmetric in evidentiary weight: Account One (AR-005) has the broadest sourcing including one independently-fetched item; Account Two (AR-006) has the most specific detail and the least corroboration; Account Three (AR-007) sits between them, agreeing with Account Two's substance but not its specifics, and itself uncorroborated.
determinations: The balance of evidence has shifted toward some affirmative resolution having been passed (Accounts Two and Three, and the subsequent conduct), but Account Two's specific resolution numbers and 9/0 vote count remain the case's single least-corroborated significant claim.
paths.boundary: Does not resolve CTR-0001. The signed confirmed minutes have not been obtained by this case at any point across seven runs and two case-creation passes.

paths.title: The October 2025 Report-Back Absence — Confirmed Across Every Source
analysis: Independent of which of the three meeting accounts is accurate, no item on Bellbrook flying-fox management appears in the October 2025 council agenda or, per every source in this case that addresses it, the confirmed minutes (EV-0001, EV-0003, EV-0005). This is described in this case's own register as "the most consistently repeated fact in the whole document set" (EV-0005's own investigation_relevance).
determinations: Whichever account of the May resolution is accurate, the specific October report-back component of it did not occur - this is the one fact in the meeting/report-back cluster corroborated by every document that addresses the period, not merely by the operator's advocacy material.
paths.boundary: States only the October absence, not its legal character (see AR-010 for the weaker, extended claim, and AR-006/AR-008 for why this path does not adopt the "non-execution of a unanimous directive" framing on its own).

paths.title: The Extended November/December 2025 and February 2026 Absence — Single-Source Claim
analysis: The Hardened Submission Package extends the report-back absence to the November and December 2025, and February 2026 meeting cycles as well (EV-0005). Unlike the October absence (AR-009), this extended claim is not independently cross-checked against those specific agendas by any other document in this case - it is carried in the same source that also supplies Account Two's uncorroborated resolution numbers (AR-006).
determinations: The extended multi-cycle absence claim should be treated with the same caution as Account Two's resolution numbers - plausible and consistent with the confirmed October absence, but not independently verified meeting-by-meeting the way the October absence is.
paths.boundary: Does not dispute the claim - only notes it has not received the same cross-source confirmation as the October absence specifically.

paths.title: The 18 March 2026 Council Letter — Item-by-Item Content Analysis
analysis: Council's letter to Bellbrook residents, signed by Caro Szary, Group Manager Strategic and Asset Planning (EV-0004), makes six distinct claims of activity: (1) correspondence to NSW DCCEEW, (2) correspondence to Mid North Coast Local Health District, (3) the 2025 community meeting, (4) the September 2025 door-knocking, (5) ongoing camp monitoring, (6) a letter of support to Bellbrook Public School, and states an intention to (7) seek external grants and (8) request state-level support via Michael Kemp MP.

Of these eight items, two are independently cross-referenced elsewhere in this case's chronology (the community meeting, CHR-0004; the door-knocking, CHR-0005). The remaining six - both correspondence items, the monitoring, the school letter, and both stated intentions - are described only in this one letter, not independently sighted or corroborated by any other document.
determinations: The letter documents a real and specific set of activities, two of which have independent chronological corroboration - but discloses no outcome for any of the eight items, and no commitment to the one instrument (a management plan) this case's central finding identifies as the actual funding precondition (AR-002).
paths.boundary: Does not claim the six uncorroborated items are false - only that they rest on Council's own account alone, which is a different evidentiary status than the two chronologically cross-referenced items.

paths.title: Level 1/Level 2 Management Actions Under the Code of Practice
analysis: The NSW Flying-fox Camp Management Code of Practice 2018 pre-approves certain Level 1 (routine site management, hygiene cleaning, signage) and Level 2 (vegetation buffer creation, branch trimming) interventions without individual licensing, subject to welfare-based scheduling conditions such as trimming only after animals depart to forage (EV-0012). Protected-species status prevents dispersal or lethal control of the colony itself; it is described as not preventing these specific lower-tier actions.
determinations: Legal protection of the species does not, on this description, by itself explain an absence of any interim Level 1/Level 2 action at the site.
paths.boundary: This description has not yet been checked against the primary Code of Practice text itself (Q-0007) - it rests on two cross-corroborating but secondary operator-supplied documents, not a directly-sighted regulatory instrument.

paths.title: The Operator's Commonwealth Registration Attempt
analysis: On 18 June 2026 at 9:56am, the operator emailed speciespolicy@dcceew.gov.au, cc'ing Paul Hodgson (the same Bellbrook Hall and Progress Association member named in EV-0001), formally notifying the Department of the Bellbrook camp and requesting assistance arranging a formal species count/census (EV-0022). The operator separately confirmed this was a deliberate registration attempt, made after learning any member of the public could submit one. This is the case's first confirmed-sent advocacy action with a dated send record, distinct from the four still-unconfirmed drafted submissions (see AR-021).
determinations: This is the only advocacy action in this case's register with both a confirmed send date and a confirmed substantive reply - a materially different evidentiary category from any of the four drafted-but-unconfirmed submissions.
paths.boundary: Does not itself establish anything about the camp's registration status - only that the attempt was made and dated.

paths.title: DCCEEW's Reply — Substantive Content Analysis
analysis: DCCEEW's direct reply (Sam Horton, Senior Policy Officer, Species Listing, Information and Policy Section, EV-0023) makes four distinct claims: (1) the National Flying Fox Monitoring Program was a collaboration between national, state/territory governments, CSIRO, local governments and community volunteers; (2) it was paused in 2022 due to cessation of federal funding; (3) the Department is not currently monitoring flying-fox camps under it and cannot send resources to survey the Bellbrook camp; (4) grey-headed flying-foxes remain federally protected, and any camp exceeding the 'nationally important camp' threshold would still need referral, with a recommendation to engage the relevant state government instead.
This is a primary institutional source responding directly to a dated, confirmed action by this case's own operator - the single hardest fact in the entire register.
determinations: The Commonwealth camp-registration/monitoring pathway is confirmed non-functional for a new camp via this specific route, independent of anything Kempsey Shire Council has or has not done - grounded in direct institutional correspondence, not inference.
paths.boundary: Does not establish whether Bellbrook meets the 'nationally important camp' threshold that would trigger referral regardless of the pause - see AR-015.

paths.title: The EPBC 'Nationally Important Camp' Threshold — Unresolved
analysis: DCCEEW's reply (EV-0023) states that a camp exceeding the EPBC Act's 'nationally important camp' threshold would still require referral, independent of the paused monitoring program. Nothing in this case's register establishes the size, density, or any other threshold-relevant characteristic of the Bellbrook colony against that specific test.
determinations: This is a genuinely open, distinct question from the monitoring-program pause (AR-014) - a live referral obligation could exist regardless of the pause, and this case's register currently contains no basis to assess it either way.
paths.boundary: Q-0011 remains fully open. This path does not speculate about the likely outcome of an assessment this case has no data to perform.

paths.title: The 'Historic' Classification Claim
analysis: The media pitch document states Council's website classifies Bellbrook as a 'historic' flying-fox camp (EV-0009) - a single-source claim when first recorded, not repeated in any of the other seven original documents. Later operator-relayed research (EV-0016) restates this and adds that Rudder Park is described as Council's only permanent camp and that Council states it cannot manage colonies on private or Crown land - with partial independent corroboration via an unrelated search snippet (found while searching NSW Parliament Hansard on a different query) that consistently used the words 'historic flying-fox camp location'.
determinations: The 'historic' classification claim has moved from single-source (EV-0009) to partially independently corroborated (EV-0016) across this case's runs - but 'partially corroborated by an unrelated search' is a materially weaker evidentiary status than a direct, dated sighting of the page itself.
paths.boundary: Does not establish whether the classification is currently accurate or stale - see AR-018 for the real, confirmed 2021 departure that provides a plausible innocent explanation this path does not rule out.

paths.title: The Unlocated June 2026 Severity Report
analysis: Operator-relayed research states a June 2026 report described the Bellbrook camp as severely affecting residents - the park reportedly unusable, waste affecting public areas, impacts on Bellbrook Public School children, residents still seeking intervention (EV-0015). An extensive independent search across the Macleay Argus, ABC Mid North Coast, Mirage News, NSW Parliament Hansard and the June 2026 Kempsey council meeting wrap found no trace of it.
determinations: This claim cannot currently be treated as established - not because it has been contradicted, but because this case has been unable to locate the source it is attributed to despite a genuine, multi-source search attempt.
paths.boundary: Non-location is not disproof. If the operator can supply the specific citation, this path should be revisited in a later pass rather than the claim being treated as settled either way in the meantime.

paths.title: The 2021 Departure Record and Chronology Coherence
analysis: Council's own 27 October 2021 page reports the colony left Bellbrook that year as weather warmed, with Bellbrook Playground subsequently cleaned and reopened; the article also states Council was aware of impacts earlier that year but could not interfere with the colony due to its protected status (EV-0013). This was independently found while attempting to verify the 'historic' classification claim, and was not previously in this case's register.

This complicates, rather than confirms or refutes, the case's own working framing that the colony has been 'continuous since November 2019' (CHR-0001). If the colony genuinely left in 2021 and only later returned, that is a materially different history than uninterrupted presence - and would provide a real, non-inaccurate basis for a 'historic' classification, if the colony has not since returned.
determinations: This case's own chronology (CHR-0001's 'continuous since 2019' framing) and this independently-found record (a confirmed 2021 departure) are not yet reconciled - this is an internal coherence gap in the case's own record, not merely an external dispute with Council.
paths.boundary: Does not determine whether the colony returned after 2021, or when. Q-0008 remains open.

paths.title: Histoplasmosis Mechanism — Real, Unconfirmed Locally
analysis: Histoplasmosis, a fungal lung/bloodstream infection from inhaling spores in accumulated droppings, is described as a real, medically documented mechanism under heavy direct droppings accumulation - distinguishable from the standard 'low risk from a distance' messaging calibrated for colonies without direct droppings contact (EV-0008). The source document explicitly notes no lab test has confirmed Histoplasma capsulatum in this specific colony's droppings, and that an absence of confirmed local cases does not mean no mild or undiagnosed infections have occurred, citing literature suggesting undiagnosed rates as high as 90% in immunocompetent people.
determinations: A real, medically documented health-risk mechanism exists in principle for heavy direct droppings exposure; no local case is confirmed, and the source material itself explicitly frames this as a scope limitation rather than a claim about anyone's intent.
paths.boundary: Must not be read as evidence any Bellbrook resident has been sickened - the source item and this path both explicitly limit the claim to mechanism, not confirmed instance (Q-0006).

paths.title: ABLV Bite/Scratch Mechanism — Real, Unconfirmed Locally, Distinct Pathway
analysis: Australian bat lyssavirus (ABLV) is a real, medically serious bite/scratch transmission risk - potentially fatal, causing paralysis, delirium and convulsions, with four deaths recorded nationally since 1996 (EV-0018, reporting a rise in North Queensland exposures, flagged by the operator as relevant background rather than a Bellbrook-specific claim). Mid North Coast Local Health District's own general public health guidance independently confirms the standard precautions: avoid handling injured or dead flying foxes, contact wildlife rescue services, wash any bite/scratch wound for 15 minutes and seek immediate medical attention (EV-0019, the only ABLV-related item in this case independently fetched and read in full).
determinations: This is a distinct exposure pathway and disease from the droppings-based histoplasmosis risk (AR-019) - different mechanism, different route, same underlying point: a real medical risk exists independent of any confirmed local case, and the two should not be conflated into one generic 'health risk' finding.
paths.boundary: EV-0018 is not Bellbrook-, Kempsey- or even NSW-specific - North Queensland exposure circumstances differ from Bellbrook's documented droppings-contamination concern. This case has no evidence of any Bellbrook-specific bite or scratch exposure (Q-0010).

paths.title: The Four Drafted-but-Unconfirmed Advocacy Submissions
analysis: Four formal documents were drafted for simultaneous lodgement, all with unsigned "Resident of Bellbrook NSW 2440" signature blocks as at case creation: a council submission with five direct questions to CEO Andrew Meddle (EV-0006), an NSW Ombudsman complaint under the Ombudsman Act 1974 (EV-0007), and a senator letter and media pitch referenced in the same drafting round. None has a confirmed lodgement date or any confirmed response in this case's register.
determinations: These four documents represent the advocacy chain's intended next step, not a completed action - a materially different evidentiary category from the operator's own confirmed-sent, confirmed-answered Commonwealth registration email (AR-013).
paths.boundary: Does not assume the four drafts were never sent - only that this case's register does not confirm they were (Q-0005).

paths.title: Evidentiary Weight Distribution Across the Register
analysis: Of the 23 evidence items in this case's frozen register, 5 are independently confirmed Verified (EV-0001, EV-0018, EV-0019, EV-0020, EV-0021). The remaining 18 are Requires Verification/Unverified, and within that group the sourcing itself varies materially: some are cross-corroborated across multiple operator-supplied documents (e.g. EV-0002, EV-0011, EV-0012), some rest on a single operator-supplied document (EV-0008, EV-0009), and four (EV-0013 aside, which is independently found and Verified-adjacent in method though formally Requires Verification) rest on operator-relayed research supplied without a citation as at the point of recording (EV-0014, EV-0015, EV-0016, and in part EV-0017).
determinations: This case's evidentiary base is not uniform in reliability even within the shared 'Requires Verification' label - treating every Unverified item as interchangeable would itself be a form of the generic flattening this analysis is built to avoid.
paths.boundary: This is a meta-analytical observation about the register's own composition, not a new factual finding about Bellbrook or Council.

cross_path_observations.title: The plan mechanism is demonstrated, not exotic
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-001, AR-003 and AR-004 converge: the management-plan instrument is actively operated inside Kempsey Shire itself (Rudder Park), actively revised by a comparable regional council (Townsville), and specifically funded for development elsewhere (Mount Isa). No single path alone shows all three; together they remove 'this is a rare or unfunded mechanism' as an available explanation for Bellbrook's absence of one.

cross_path_observations.title: Three accounts, three different evidentiary weights
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-005, AR-006, AR-007 and AR-008 together show the meeting-account dispute is not a simple two-sided contradiction - it is three accounts with three distinct sourcing profiles, only one of which (AR-006) supplies the specific numbers this case's strongest remedy language would need, and that one is also the least corroborated.

cross_path_observations.title: The report-back gap has a confirmed core and an unconfirmed extension
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-009 and AR-010 together show this case should not treat 'no report-back through February 2026' as a single fact of uniform confidence - the October 2025 absence is cross-source confirmed; the extension through November, December and February is currently single-source.

cross_path_observations.title: One Commonwealth channel, two distinct open questions
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-013, AR-014 and AR-015 together show the Commonwealth registration attempt produced one hard confirmed fact (the program's pause) and left one genuinely separate question open (the EPBC threshold) - these should not be treated as a single resolved 'Commonwealth pathway is dead' finding.

cross_path_observations.title: Three independent strands, no single conclusive one
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-016, AR-017 and AR-018 each bear on whether Bellbrook's camp is accurately described as 'historic' - a partially-corroborated classification claim, an unlocated severity report, and a confirmed real 2021 departure that could fully explain the classification without inaccuracy. No single strand is conclusive; read together they show why CTR-0002 remains genuinely, not just formally, open.

cross_path_observations.title: Two health mechanisms, not one 'health risk' finding
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-019 and AR-020 are structurally distinct risks (fungal, droppings-borne vs. viral, bite/scratch-borne) that a less granular pass would have compressed into a single generic 'health risk exists' path - keeping them separate preserves the different evidentiary bases each actually has.

cross_path_observations.title: One confirmed action stands apart from four unconfirmed drafts
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-013 and AR-021 together show this case's advocacy record is not a uniform set of 'things the operator tried' - one action (Commonwealth registration) has a confirmed send date and a confirmed reply; four (council, Ombudsman, senator, media) remain unconfirmed drafts. Conflating them would overstate what has actually been attempted.

disclosure_requests.title: Signed confirmed minutes, 20 May 2025 Kempsey Shire Council ordinary meeting
disclosure_requests.request: The primary record needed to resolve CTR-0001 and Q-0001 - which of the three accounts (AR-005, AR-006, AR-007) is accurate, including whether Resolution 2025.79/2025.80 and the stated 9/0 vote and defeated 2/7 amendment are real.

disclosure_requests.title: Current text of Council's flying-fox webpage
disclosure_requests.request: A dated, directly-sighted capture of the page's full text - the 'historic' classification, the Rudder Park comparison, and the private/Crown land management claims - needed to resolve Q-0004, Q-0009 and CTR-0002.

disclosure_requests.title: NSW Government flying-fox camp management grants program guidelines
disclosure_requests.request: The program's own published eligibility terms, to confirm or correct the operator-supplied claim analysed in AR-002 that a completed or draft Camp Management Plan is a strict funding precondition.

disclosure_requests.title: NSW Flying-fox Camp Management Code of Practice 2018 (primary text)
disclosure_requests.request: To confirm the Level 1/Level 2 management actions described in AR-012 against the Code's actual text.

contradictions_preserved.issue: Three distinct accounts of the 20 May 2025 council meeting remain in tension - see AR-005 through AR-008 for the full triangulation.
contradictions_preserved.analysis: Not resolved by this analysis - the signed confirmed minutes have not been obtained across seven runs and two case-creation passes.

contradictions_preserved.issue: Council's current 'historic' classification may or may not match a functional 2026 reality of severe, ongoing impact - see AR-016 through AR-018 for the three independent strands bearing on this.
contradictions_preserved.analysis: Not resolved by this analysis - the June 2026 report has not been located and it is not established whether the colony returned after its confirmed 2021 departure.

overreach_controls: No claim is made about why Kempsey Shire Council has not produced a Bellbrook-specific management plan - only that it has not, against a mechanism it operates elsewhere in the same shire.
No intent is attributed to any individual councillor, council officer, or Commonwealth official at any point in this analysis - every finding describes documented institutional record, not motive.

AR-006 and AR-008 do not adopt the Hardened Submission Package's characterisation of council's conduct as non-execution of an affirmative unanimous directive - that characterisation depends on the unresolved CTR-0001 and is not treated as established here.

AR-016 through AR-018 do not present the 'historic' classification as inaccurate or as a confirmed documented-vs-functional gap - CTR-0002 remains genuinely open, with a real alternative explanation (the 2021 departure, AR-018) not yet ruled out.

AR-019 and AR-020 do not claim any Bellbrook resident has experienced histoplasmosis or an ABLV exposure - both are stated as real mechanisms without a confirmed local instance, matching the source evidence's own explicit hedge.

This pass deliberately does not compress distinct claims of different evidentiary weight into single generic findings (see AR-022 and every cross-path observation above) - the prior nine-path pass's central failure was doing exactly that, and is not repeated here.

This is Pass 1 of an explicitly ongoing process. It is not represented as exhaustive relative to future passes, and no downstream stage should be built from it until the operator states DFAPTA itself is frozen.
